newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson Multimedia set for big profits.
newsitem.headline: Thomson Multimedia set for big profits.

text.p: Thomson Multimedia, the loss-making state consumer electronics group set to be sold to Daewoo Electronics for one franc, will be structurally profitable from 1999 at the latest, sources said on Friday.
Industrial sources said that while the group, fully-owned by Thomson SA, made a loss in the first half, technology licences would bring in a billion francs ($192 million) a year from 1999.
The French government on Wednesday said it had decided to sell state-owned Thomson SA for one franc to Lagardere Groupe after an 11 billion franc cash injection.
Lagardere wants to merge its Matra defence unit with Thomson's Thomson-CSF and will hive off Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo of South Korea.
Thomson Multimedia is the world's fourth-biggest television set company and the biggest such group in the U.S. with brand names as RCA, Saba and Thomson and others.

The group has been heavily involved, and massively invested, in the development of digital television and is a leader in decoder technology as well as a member of the Digital Video Disc (DVD) consortium.
Due to fierce competition from Asian giants, relatively expensive production lines and weak consumer markets, Thomson Multimedia is in the red.

An industrial source said the company lost three billion francs in the first half of 1996. This figure is made up by a one billion franc operating loss, a 1.2 billion franc restructuring charge and 800 million in interest charges.
Thomson Multimedia had no comment on the figures.

This situation is set to change dramatically. The group was already working on a restructuring, closing eight production sites in the United States, Germany and southeast Asia and cutting 5,000 of 49,500 jobs, mainly outside France.

The operating loss could disappear in the second half due to the seasonallity of sales in consumer electronics, with the December gift season and end-of-year salary bonuses skewing sales towards the last months of the year.
On top of that, Thomson will get money from technology licences from the 1987 buy of RCA from General Electric.
"At the time, Thomson paid a low price for RCA but granted General Electric the right to revenues of existing and pending technology licences until 1998," a company official said.
But after 1998, the portfolio of licences will yield at least a billion francs per year.

At the Finance Ministry there was no comment on the figure of one billion francs in licence income from 1999, but officials stressed that both bidders for Thomson SA -- Lagardere and Alcatel Alsthom -- had access to all financial information including the patent and licence situation.
"The figure, whatever it is, has been taken into account in the valuation of Thomson which leads to a recapitalisation of 11 billion francs," the official said.
Thomson Multimedia workers and labour unions expressed their anger about being sold at the cheap to a South Korean company.
The CGT labour union said that "taxpayers are going to cough up 11 billion francs so that a minuscule Korean company can get French technologies of the future".
Researcher Eddie Cohen, a specialist in industrial policy, said in Le Monde that Daewoo was mainly known as "a maker of low-end products, a technology follower, without development resources."
Daewoo Electronics chairman Bae Soon-hoon said in Seoul on Thursday that the company would pay one franc for Thomson Multimedia and expected part of the capital injection.
He said Daewoo would create 5,000 jobs at Thomson Multimedia, of which he will become chief executive officer. ($1=5.207 French Franc)
